summary: Docs-only deliverable (PR #487, merged 5448c1a4): 4 files (PROGRESS.md, ai-os/OS.yaml, new v2 plan, ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml), 470 add / 30 del, no code/schema/auth/RLS/workflow files touched. The v2 plan is a well-grounded re-scoring of the 2045-row CSV against actually-shipped work — it cites live-verified code paths (schema.ts line numbers, real API routes, merged PR #s) for its 'already shipped' claims rather than asserting them. It is appropriately conservative where it counts: money-blocked rows (SOC2, pentest, live payment-gateway merchant account, paid training content, Supabase IPv4) are explicitly KEPT deferred since decision authority does not extend to spending; V2-5 (BYOB AI-model) states 'Never bypass checkTierEligibility()' (Rule 9); every schema-touching downstream task is flagged tier2 for human hold; the gh-token workflow-scope limitation is disclosed for V2-7 rather than attempting a push that would be rejected. Top-level accounting reconciles (188+1610=1798 closed; 42+33=75 deferred set; 22+13+40=75 decision split). One internal doc-quality inconsistency (bucket (a)'s '22 deferred' vs its own per-row breakdown summing to 11 — the training split is stated as 7/7 in the table but 18-deferred in the footnote) is flagged below but does not undermine the deliverable's soundness as a planning artifact. No .github/workflows/** files are modified; the hard rule is respected.
issues: Internal arithmetic inconsistency in the decision log's bucket (a) composition: §2(a) is titled '22 rows stay deferred' but its own per-row breakdown sums to 11 (2 SOC2/audit #09/#08 + 2 payment-gateway #69/#72 + 7 of 14 training rows, per the table's explicit 7/7 split). The reconciling footnote claims '18 training where the paid-content half is deferred' (=22), contradicting the table's '14 rows split 7 deferred / 7 decided'. The 7-vs-18 training-deferred count needs reconciling before downstream dispatch feeds the §3 status flips to gap_queue.yaml (V2-25), since an over- or under-count of deferred training rows would mis-route rows that are actually decidable. Doc-quality issue only; no code/security impact.
